newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian pre-Easter wool prices seen firm.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian pre-Easter wool prices seen firm.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to remain stable at auctions in Sydney, Geelong and Fremantle this week when about 82,700 bales will be offered, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said in its weekly market preview.
Despite initial signs of weakness in the past week, the market held well toward the close, it said.
This surprised, given relatively quiet Chinese trading which traditionally supports the broad wool market, it said.
Instead, a broad cross-section of traders last week appeared to be buying for prompt shipment and indent orders to replenish stocks in anticipation of a dearer market, it said.
This was an encouraging sign for this week's market and was expected to prevent further weakness in prices, it said.
"However, generally, stabilisation is predicted with any upturn restricted by increased quantities for sale with the latest upward revision of the selling roster," it said.
Up to 10 percent more wool than expected will be for sale in the next two weeks, it said.
Also, the strengthening Australian dollar was not assisting buying activity, it said.
"So a period of price stabilisation is expected through the Easter recess," it said.

The Australian Council of Wool Exporters said topmaker needs to keep processing machinery in operation could inject a positive note to the market this week, with only two weeks remaining before the Easter recess.
But if the 110,000 bales currently estimated for offering in the last week before Easter did eventuate, it would test the underlying strength of the market, ACWE said.
The two-week recess begins the week starting March 24.
Last week the eastern market indicator fell two cents a kg clean to 622 cents a kg clean.
